title: Soft Shield
warm:
Brooks leaned hard and [player_name] became the soft shield for Nolan Greer in lobby light that made every neighbor look like cover. Soft alibi as public posture. Early thirties. Across the hall. Detective Imani Brooks's homicide interest rising—questions about last known, about sandbagging, about why Vivienne's perfume still sat unused if travel were true—without a body placed on any table. Four fates contested on purpose in [player_name]'s mouth.

"She was thinning her visits before I ever crossed his door with intent," [player_name] said carefully. "Weekly to monthly to gone is cadence I lived beside, not a corpse I built. Soft shield is not confession of murder. Soft shield is refusal to let your colder file invent endings for a woman who may have left, been paid, died, or staged."

Nolan stood half a step behind her—cufflinks quiet, brutal charm banked. Marcus Pell watched from marble distance. Rhea's desk blank. Elevator chime. Wind sheer. Black car. Wine memory. Shielding cost something; [player_name] felt it in her throat.

Brooks's eyes flicked between them. "Shields crack. When yours does, I will be here. Until then—take your silence war upstairs and refuse his mouth while you stay useful, or chase the holding-badge number behind your shield and find out whose politics you are actually wearing."

[player_name] tasted lobby air and unfinished want. Soft shield could refuse intimacy tonight—silence war as discipline—or hunt internal badge shadow while still standing between Nolan and the law.

She catalogued what Crownspire still offered as soft machinery: elevator chime late at night, wine glass ring on marble, Vivienne's unused perfume in a bath she should not know, black car idling at the curb, Brooks's badge flash in the lobby, Nolan's cufflinks clicking when he lied, Rhea's slate with thinning marks, wind sheer against floor-to-ceiling glass. Anchors rotated through the hour without stacking into elegant absolutes. Dialogue had already carried the subtext; the anchors only kept score. Hope and dread shared every doorway. Vivienne's willing leave, paid vanish, death, or staging remained L10-open on purpose—Layer 5 only allowed homicide interest to rise, never a settled corpse to end the wanting or the dread. [player_name] felt the soft alibi's remaining give and understood consequence would spend it either way.

Soft shield public posture required [player_name] to speak cadence without offering endings, to stand between Nolan and Brooks without becoming a second detective or a second wife. Lobby light was unforgiving. Soft answers preferred by money sounded thinner each time Brooks refused traveling as liturgy. Silence war upstairs would discipline desire into strategy. Holding-badge chase behind the shield would smuggle investigation under loyalty. Both kept Vivienne contested. Both admitted homicide interest had changed the temperature of every across-the-hall knock.
hot:
Soft shield in lobby light made [player_name]'s body a public instrument—early thirties, across-the-hall, nipples tight under silk because refusing Brooks meant standing so close to Nolan she could feel his heat without claiming it. Homicide tilt. No corpse. Vivienne contested. Mid-want screaming behind soft posture.

Silence war upstairs meant denying his mouth while her cunt voted traitor. Holding-badge chase behind the shield meant politics as edging—number on her tongue, his eyes on her throat. She chose under badge flash, unfinished shield still warm.

Body-POV kept the through-line physical: pulse at throat, heat low in the belly, silk clinging, mid-want ending before climax because the next verb still owned the night. Nolan Greer only—mid-forties, finance and tech holding, brutal charm, rain-money cologne—romance lock unbroken. Crime stayed plot; intimacy stayed intimacy-forward, never gore-porn, never eroticizing absence as kink. Brooks's colder paper could press her skin; Vivienne's contested fate could press her ribs; neither turned sex into violence cosplay. [player_name] ached around unanswered questions the way Crownspire ached around a wife who might still be anywhere. Choosing hurt. Hurting meant the choice was real. Soft alibi had a pulse; Layer 5 made her feel every beat.

Standing as shield put her back nearly to his chest—heat without hug, public almost that soaked her in private. Refuse-his-mouth later would be edging as ethics. Badge-chase would be edging as plot. Soft smut under politics stayed Nolan-only, body-POV, mid-want locked. She held the posture until choosing cracked it.
